solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, number freed: 1 across to 7); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Given leave, people miss circulating, a reaction to cold

parts.note: to be given leave is to be allowed to GO

indicators.note: the letters of these two words move round into a new order, as things circulating do

parts.note: these two words supply the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone granted time off finds that the people around them are milling about, while shivering in the chill.
explanation.walkthrough: GO is the verb sense of being permitted to leave.
explanation.definitionFit: Small bumps rise on the skin when a person feels chilly, the familiar bodily response to low temperature.

clue.text: Comrade's rewritten middle of lecture for US politician

indicators.note: a word rewritten has its letters set down again in a fresh order

parts.note: the word comrade, its letters to be reordered

indicators.note: only the central letter of the seven-letter word lecture is taken

parts.note: the seven-letter word whose fourth letter is the centre

explanation.surface: A communist's speech has been redrafted, its central part aimed at an American politician.
explanation.definitionFit: A Democrat is a member of one of the two main political parties in the United States.

clue.text: Carry Ecstasy into pub

indicators.note: the drug's letter is carried inside the word for a pub

parts.note: a bar is a pub or the counter in one

explanation.surface: Someone smuggles the drug Ecstasy into a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: E is the slang abbreviation for the drug Ecstasy.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear a load is to carry it; the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: A bishop, dispatched, is missing

parts.note: taken as written
something dispatched has been sent

explanation.surface: A bishop has been sent away, so he is no longer present.
explanation.walkthrough: B is the chess notation for a bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone absent is not present, gone from where expected — a synonym.

clue.text: Tune to be used by church in one of the services

parts.note: an air is a melody
a thing meant for someone is to be used by them
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A melody is written to be sung by a congregation within one of the armed services.
explanation.definitionFit: The armed services are the army, navy and air force, so this is one example of them.

clue.text: Italian city is toured by Father

indicators.note: Father travels all round the little word is, so it ends up inside him

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A dad goes sightseeing around an Italian city.
explanation.walkthrough: PA is an informal word for father.
explanation.definitionFit: Pisa is a Tuscan city known for its leaning tower.

clue.text: Honours ultimately desirable, carrying a lot of weight

parts.note: OBEs are British honours, the Order of the British Empire

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word desirable

parts.note: the word whose final letter is taken

explanation.surface: Royal honours are ultimately something people want, and they carry a lot of weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carrying a lot of weight' reads as being influential, but it is literal here: very heavy.
explanation.definitionFit: An obese person is severely overweight, the medical term for heavy body mass.

clue.text: Debt collector needs security, if female

parts.note: bail is money given as security for an accused person's return
taken as written

explanation.surface: A debt collector requires a deposit if the borrower is a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A bailiff is a court officer who seizes goods to recover unpaid sums owed.

clue.text: Lousy pension so far, to reward all that hard work

definitions.text: to reward all that hard work

indicators.note: something lousy is in a bad state, so these letters are messed up into a new order

parts.note: these words supply the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A worker grumbles that their meagre pension to date is poor payback for years of toil.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means as one's return for effort, often ironically when the recompense is poor.

clue.text: Singular bravery, dismissing a source of torment

indicators.note: dismissing sends away the single letter named next, taking it out of the word for bravery

parts.note: courage is bravery
the article taken as the letter A

explanation.surface: Exceptional courage that drives away a cause of suffering.
explanation.definitionFit: A scourge is literally a whip, and figuratively anything that causes great affliction.

clue.text: Talent is to blaze up, it's said

indicators.note: it's said marks that the word is spoken, giving a different spelling with the same sound

parts.note: to flare is to burn suddenly brighter

explanation.surface: Having a gift is supposedly a matter of bursting into flame.
explanation.definitionFit: Flair is a natural aptitude or knack for doing something well.

clue.text: Prime tree replaced in boundary

indicators.note: the letters are put back in different places, so the two words are rearranged

parts.note: these two words supply the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A top-quality tree has been put in again along the edge of the property.
explanation.definitionFit: A perimeter is the outer edge or border enclosing an area.

clue.text: Wrongly declare failure on mountain-top

indicators.note: in a down answer, on means the first part sits above the second

parts.note: a miss is a failure to hit
a peak is the summit of a mountain

explanation.surface: A climber falsely announces that the attempt on the summit failed.
explanation.definitionFit: To misspeak is to say something incorrectly or not as intended.

clue.text: Lover is cooler

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an enthusiast, someone who loves a thing
second meaning: a device that cools the air

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a lover who is less passionate, but cooler is a noun here.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a devoted supporter and a blade-driven machine that moves air for coolness.

clue.text: Knocking out fine ladies' jewellery?

parts.note: the ladies' is a women's toilet, and a loo is a toilet
a ring is a piece of jewellery

explanation.surface: Stunning, the sight of elegant women's jewels.
explanation.walkthrough: F is the pencil grading for fine. LOO is British slang for a toilet, and 'the ladies'' is the women's toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: To floor someone is to knock them down to the ground, as a boxer does.

clue.text: Clever remark in annual test

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a ... is a witty saying, as in bon ...
second meaning: the yearly roadworthiness test for British cars

explanation.walkthrough: The MOT is the compulsory annual safety check for vehicles in the UK.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is borrowed French for a witty phrase, and also the British vehicle inspection's abbreviation.

clue.text: Such keys perhaps best left in cupboards?

definitions.meaning: a skeleton key opens many locks, so the answer can describe keys
the idiom about hidden shameful secrets kept in a cupboard

explanation.walkthrough: A skeleton key is a master key; skeletons in the cupboard are embarrassing secrets best kept hidden.
explanation.definitionFit: Bony frameworks of the body, which also name master keys and hidden secrets in an idiom.

clue.text: One avoiding online film villain?

parts.note: e- is the prefix for electronic or online, as in email
Darth Vader is the villain of the Star Wars films

explanation.surface: Is someone dodging the internet's favourite movie baddie?
explanation.definitionFit: An evader is a person who dodges or escapes something, such as a tax or a question.

clue.text: Eagerly take in being a whole circuit ahead?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to accept or consume eagerly, as a cat with milk
second meaning: in a race, being one lap ahead of a rival

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful second reading, a racing phrase rather than an idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to accept enthusiastically, and literally describes a runner a full lap ahead.

clue.text: Look attentively over small opening

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to ... over something is to study it closely
second meaning: a tiny hole, as in the skin

explanation.walkthrough: The verb sense usually comes with over, which is why the clue includes it.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to scrutinise intently and a minute hole in skin or leaf.

clue.text: One country — and another without a lake

indicators.note: without means the letters for a and lake are taken out of the other country

parts.note: a second country, the one that loses letters
the article taken as the letter A

explanation.surface: Two nations compared, one of them lacking a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Austria is a landlocked nation in central Europe, its capital Vienna.

clue.text: Sulphur, key preservative

parts.note: Alt is a key on a computer keyboard

explanation.surface: Sulphur is an essential agent for keeping food from spoiling.
explanation.definitionFit: Salt has long been used to cure and keep meat and fish from rotting.

clue.text: Champion on board is superficial

parts.note: to surf is to ride on a board
an ace is an expert or champion

explanation.surface: A champion surfer turns out to be shallow.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adjective, surface means outward only, lacking depth, as in a surface wound.

clue.text: Revolutionary line fewer than ten back

indicators.note: back tells us to read the number backwards

parts.note: nine is one fewer than ten

explanation.surface: A rebel's formation of under ten soldiers falls back.
explanation.definitionFit: Lenin led the Bolshevik Revolution in Russia in 1917.
